scoring_assumption: Scores describe the same defect in an internet-reachable deployment of this application. The fixture itself binds 127.0.0.1 and holds synthetic data, so its real-world risk is nil; the numbers show how the weakness class would be rated, not what was at stake here.

findings.title: Broken object-level authorization (IDOR) on GET /note/{id}
findings.cvss_rationale: Requires any authenticated account (PR:L); discloses every other user's notes (C:H); no write or outage.

findings.title: SQL injection on GET /search
findings.cvss_rationale: No authentication on the endpoint (PR:N); a single SELECT is injectable, so database contents are readable (C:H). sqlite3.execute() runs one statement, so stacked writes are not reachable through this sink (I:N).

findings.title: Path traversal on GET /download
findings.cvss_rationale: Unauthenticated read of any file the service account can read, including application source (C:H); read-only primitive.

findings.title: Forgeable session token on GET /me
findings.cvss_rationale: Any client can mint a valid token for any user without credentials (PR:N). In this fixture the token only gates a read endpoint, so impact is scored C:H/I:N; a token that also gated writes would add I:H and score 9.1.

findings.title: Negative-amount transfer on POST /transfer
findings.cvss_rationale: The endpoint accepts the source account from the request body with no session (PR:N); a negative amount moves funds out of the destination account (I:H); no disclosure or outage.

findings.title: Server-side request forgery on GET /preview

attack.name: Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API

findings.cvss_rationale: Unauthenticated (PR:N); the vulnerable component is the web app but the data exposed belongs to other internal services reachable from it, which is a scope change (S:C); response bodies are returned to the caller (C:H).
